Sri Krishna Restaurant is a place I’ve visited a few times over the years, and it continues to be a dependable option in the Mumbai dining scene, especially for South Indian vegetarian food.

One of the standout items here, in my experience, is the Dahi Vada, which I’ve had on multiple occasions and would definitely recommend. It’s consistently well-prepared and enjoyable.

On my most recent order, I also tried the Medu Vada and Rava Masala Dosa. While the food overall was good, I wasn’t particularly impressed with the sambar that accompanied the vada. Since sambar plays a key role in the dish, this did affect the overall experience for me. The rest of the preparation, however, was satisfactory.

They also offer a variety of ice creams, and the mango option we tried was quite good and made for a nice finish to the meal.

Service here is excellent. The staff are attentive and helpful, with waiters proactively suggesting dishes and offering recommendations in a thoughtful, non-pushy manner and something that enhances the overall dining experience.

The restaurant is purely vegetarian and has a cool, calm, comfortable ambience, making it suitable for a quiet, relaxed lunch or dinner.

Overall, Sri Krishna remains a reliable and recommended spot, particularly for its strengths in select dishes and service.

featured_reviews.name: sagar jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was my third visit to Santosham, and it continues to be a great spot for comforting, authentic South Indian food!
If you are looking for a complete traditional experience, their unlimited South Indian Thali is a must-try at least once. It’s a beautifully simple, home-style meal that tastes amazing. The thali comes fully loaded with a variety of authentic items—hot puris, steamed rice, flavorful and piping hot Sambar, a wonderfully tangy Rasam, and traditional sabjis like a dry Beans and Carrot Poriyal and a comforting Cabbage Kootu. They round it out with crisp appalams, fresh curd, pickle, and a sweet Payasam to finish it off. Just a quick heads-up: they have different pricing for the unlimited thali on weekdays versus weekends.
While the thali is fantastic and incredibly generous, it is quite a heavy meal. Personally, since we lean more toward classic South Indian snacks rather than massive authentic meals, the thali is a 'try it once for the experience' item for us.
If you aren't super hungry or just prefer lighter fare, absolutely go for their Idli and Dosa options instead. They are perfectly prepared and hit the spot every time. I also have to give a massive shoutout to their Dal Wada—it is incredibly crispy on the outside, perfectly spiced, and just flat-out delicious.

Staff is very helpful, one of the staff saw I m not adding Green chutney on rice, he came and suggested to use green chutney over the rice and it really tasted so good 😊
Overall verdict: Come hungry for the grand unlimited thali at least once, but you'll find yourself coming back regularly for the stellar dosas, idlis, and that amazing dal wada!

featured_reviews.name: RACHNA TULI MASHKARIA
featured_reviews.review_text:
The banana leaf thali is not just a meal – it’s an experience that blends flavor, tradition, and hospitality in the most wholesome way. Served on a fresh banana leaf, the thali immediately brings a sense of authenticity and connection to Indian culinary roots.

What makes it truly special is the variety. From fragrant rice and comforting dals to vibrant curries, tangy pickles, crispy papad, and a sweet finish, every dish complements the other beautifully. The balance of flavors – spicy, tangy, salty, and sweet – ensures that every bite feels satisfying. The banana leaf itself adds a subtle earthy aroma while also being eco-friendly and hygienic.

Another highlight is the cultural warmth associated with it. The way servers lovingly add refills, encouraging you to eat to your heart’s content, makes the experience feel both generous and personal.

Overall, the banana leaf thali is not just good – it’s nourishing, soulful, and a celebration of food as tradition. Whether you’re a food enthusiast or someone who loves comfort meals, it’s definitely worth trying.

featured_reviews.name: Sarah Chamdawala
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had an amazing authentic South Indian breakfast at Santosham! Ordered the Mysore sada dosa, which was crispy and spicy and delicious; the ghee podi idli was fluffy and you could really taste the shuddh ghee; the beetroot rawa dosa was soo crispy and had just the perfect little hint of beetroot flavour; the benne dosa was yum and perfectly crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside and served with the most decadent pure white butter! The filter coffees (both cold and hot) were also delicious with the perfect froth on top! We also enjoyed the rose milk with chia seeds. The tomato chutney, coconut chutney and sambhar served on the side were also great and proved the perfect accompaniments to the meal.
A special mention for the service which was top notch, thanks to Nasim and Uday who were very helpful and quick.
10/10 would recommend this place!

Vanakkam Vihar, located right opposite the iconic Royal Opera House in Girgaon, is a reliable, bustling spot for anyone craving solid, comforting South Indian comfort food in South Mumbai. Whether you are wrapping up a beach stroll at nearby Girgaon Chowpatty or stepping out after a show at the Opera House, this multi-level pure-vegetarian restaurant offers a welcoming and clean environment.
Here is a comprehensive look at what to expect:
The Vibe & Ambiance
The restaurant balances traditional charm with a modern, spacious casual-dining setup. The ground floor features comfortable high and low seating, while the upper level ("Firangi") branches out into multi-cuisine options. The space is well-lit, fully air-conditioned, and remarkably clean, making it highly family-friendly. The staff adds a touch of authenticity by dressing in traditional South Indian attire.
What to Order
While the massive menu extends to North Indian dishes and street-side snacks, the absolute highlight here remains their coastal and southern delicacies.
The Dosas: Their Kara Masala Dosa and Chettinad Dosa are beautifully crisp, served with generous portions of fresh coconut chutney, a tangy tomato-garlic chutney, and piping hot sambar. If you are looking for something lighter, the Neer Dosa and fluffy Appams paired with a rich veggie stew or Malabari curry are top-tier.
The Idli Platters: Beyond standard idlis, their Podi Idli (tossed in a vibrant, spiced gun powder and ghee) and the signature Thalaiva Idli are highly recommended.
Filter Coffee: No meal here is complete without their authentic Filter Coffee. It is served strong, perfectly frothy, and features that robust, traditional chicory-coffee blend.
Jain Options: For those with dietary restrictions, the restaurant stands out for offering a robust, dedicated selection of highly flavorful Jain South Indian variants.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Govinda's Restaurant near Chowpatty, Girgaon, and had a wonderful dining experience. What makes this place truly unique is that, being associated with the ISKCON Temple Trust, they do not use garlic or onions in any of their preparations. Despite this, the food is incredibly flavorful and satisfying, proving that great taste doesn't always need conventional ingredients.

The menu offers a wide variety of options across different cuisines. We started our meal with a selection of soups including Artichoke Bisque, Minestrone, Manchow, Tomato Lemongrass, and Laksa Soup. Each soup had a distinct flavor profile and was perfectly balanced. My personal favorite was the Artichoke Bisque Soup, as it was my first time trying it and I absolutely loved its rich, creamy texture and unique taste.

For starters, we ordered the Kung Pao Paneer and Masala Papad. The paneer was well-cooked with just the right amount of spice, while the masala papad made for a light and crunchy accompaniment.

In the main course, we enjoyed Paneer Lababdar and Dal Tadka paired with Jeera Rice. The gravies were comforting, flavorful, and complemented the rice beautifully.

The highlight of the meal was undoubtedly the Sizzling Brownie. Served hot and indulgent, it was the perfect way to end the dining experience.

Overall, Govinda's is a small yet charming restaurant with a constant flow of patrons, which speaks volumes about its popularity. If you're looking for delicious vegetarian food with a unique sattvic approach, this place is definitely worth a visit.

🔹 *Farm Fresh Pizza*: Wait, a farm-fresh pizza inside a temple? 🤯! Toppings were fresh, crust was spot on 🍕. Got the vibe that the ingredients were picked fresh for the temple devotees... felt special!

Eating amidst the temple's vibes, felt like a foodie blessing 🙌. Service was super attentive 😊.

If you're around Iskon anywhere in the world, Govinda's is an absolute MUST 📍. Blend of divine vibes + tasty food = recipe for a soulful meal 👌."

If you’re craving an authentic Gujarati feast with a seasonal twist, Gujju Bhai No Thali is absolutely worth a visit right now!

The highlight of the experience is their unlimited aamras, served fresh as a summer special—and honestly, it steals the show. Sweet, rich, and perfectly chilled, it pairs beautifully with their hot, fluffy puris… pure comfort on a plate.

The thali itself is incredibly wholesome and satisfying. It starts off with refreshing drinks like chaas and pudina pani, setting the tone for what’s to come. The appetisers—kachori, dhokla, and chaat tart—are all fresh and flavourful, giving you that perfect mix of crunch, spice, and tang.

Moving to the mains, you’re treated to four different sabjis, two dals, and a classic Gujarati kadhi that strikes the perfect balance of sweet and tangy. Pair these with soft phulkas or puris, and it’s a complete meal in itself. You also get options like jeera rice and comforting dal khichdi, which just add to the homely feel of the meal.

And just when you think you’re done, the desserts keep coming! From warm halwa to the indulgent malai sandwich, everything feels like a celebration of flavours.

Overall, Gujju Bhai No Thali delivers a hearty, value-for-money dining experience with that signature Gujarati hospitality. With the mango season in full swing, the unlimited aamras makes it even more special—definitely not to be missed!
